description: Shared Renovate preset for Corey Alan repos. Reference with: { "extends": ["github>Corey-Alan-Consulting/deploy-workflows:renovate-config"] }

hostRules.description: Read-only auth for restricted @corey-alan-consulting/* packages. NPM_READ_TOKEN is injected by the Renovate runner's secret store, never committed.

customManagers.description: BuildKit pin in setup-buildx-action driver-opts. Nothing else watches this: `driver-opts: image=moby/buildkit:<tag>` is not a dependency file, not an action ref and not a Dockerfile FROM, so every built-in manager skips it and the pin ages silently. #6's pin went three releases stale exactly this way, and #73's first cut was stale within twenty minutes of being written. Deliberately requires a numeric tag so the floating `buildx-stable-1` this pin exists to replace is never matched.

packageRules.description: Hand-curated security pins, not ordinary dependencies. In `overrides`, the KEY encodes the vulnerable range and the value is the patched floor, so Renovate reads the value as a plain range and offers the latest major — which forces that major on every transitive consumer matched by the key. On blue-skysolutions.com that turned `js-yaml@>=3.0.0 <3.15.0` into ^4.3.1, forcing @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config across the safeLoad API removal. Advisory bumps here have to be made by hand, against the advisory's own fix floor.

Third-party minor and patch updates arrive as ONE grouped, automergeable PR per repo rather than one PR per package. Placed before the first-party rule below so that rule still overrides groupName and minimumReleaseAge for @corey-alan-consulting/** — Renovate applies packageRules in order and later matches win. Why: on 2026-10-12 the fleet held 34 stale Renovate PRs and 223 open Dependabot alerts, 70 of them high or critical, runtime-scope and with a published fix. They were not ignored out of neglect; they were unmergeable with confidence, because no app PR gate compiled the app and green therefore meant 'types still check' rather than 'it still builds'. app-pr-checks v1.12.0 added that build step, which is what makes automerge here defensible at all. Majors are excluded: breaking by semver, so they keep opening individual PRs for review. Automerge assumes the consuming repo gates merges on required status checks, and it is NOT a release: the renovate-changeset workflow opens a separate changeset PR afterwards that a human still merges, so a dependency reaches production only by a deliberate act.

First-party packages: group + automerge minor/patch on green CI once a release has aged a day. Majors are breaking by semver, so they open a normal PR for human review. Automerge assumes the consuming repo gates merges on required status checks.

First-party reusable workflows / composite actions: bump the SHA pin when a new deploy-workflows release tag is cut; automerge non-major on green CI, same policy as internal packages. PROVEN 2026-10-13 why this rule looked broken for months: it was never a matcher problem. Renovate's Dependency Dashboard listed the update correctly on branch `renovate/deploy-workflows` (so matchPackageNames and groupName both applied) but filed it under `## Awaiting Schedule` on app-template and showcase, and `## Rate-Limited` on jlshaw.link. The rule inherited the root `schedule: [before 6am on monday]`, so the PR could only be raised in one ~6h window a week, and in that window it competed for the default prHourlyLimit against the much larger `non-major dependencies` group and lost. Net effect: the six app repos sat on v1.6.0 while main reached v1.12.5 -- nine minors -- so v1.8.0's generic image-scan gate and v1.10.0's migrate-scan gate were never reaching them. A gate nobody is pinned to is not running, which makes this a security control, not dependency hygiene. Hence `schedule: [at any time]` to escape the weekly window (the same escape vulnerabilityAlerts uses) and `prPriority` above the default 0 so it wins a slot when the hourly limit binds. NOTE: the earlier `digest`-update theory was a red herring -- the single autoclosed digest PR was a separate artifact, and matchUpdateTypes was never what blocked this.
Coordinate Auth.js bumps across repos while next-auth is still in beta.

Stripe never rides in the automerge group. Each stripe SDK release pins ONE exact API-version literal in its types, so even a patch-level bump inside an existing caret range forces the consuming code to adopt a new Stripe API version — and a Stripe API version change alters response shapes and webhook payloads. Observed 2026-10-12: stripe 20.1.2 -> 20.4.1, a lockfile-only minor, changed the required literal from '2025-12-15.clover' to '2026-02-25.clover' and failed coreyalan.com's build inside the 75-package non-major group. Routing it to its own ungrouped, non-automerged PR means the API-version migration is a decision someone makes rather than a side effect of dependency hygiene. Only coreyalan.com pins the literal today; the rule is here rather than in that repo because the coupling is a property of the SDK, so it will bite the next repo that pins one.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes escape every throttle above: they ignore the weekly schedule, leave the non-major group so one unrelated failure cannot hold a CVE fix hostage, and skip minimumReleaseAge entirely — a three-day soak is prudent against a compromised release and indefensible against a known-exploited one. They DO automerge, and this object deliberately does not say so. An earlier version of this comment claimed the opposite ("deliberately does NOT set automerge"), reasoning that vulnerabilityAlerts is a separate config object rather than a packageRule. That was wrong: Renovate layers vulnerabilityAlerts ON TOP of the fully-resolved config, so a security patch still matches the non-major packageRule above and inherits its automerge:true — only the four keys set here are overridden. Verified live on 2026-10-12, when coreyalan.com#265 (next 15.5.24 → 15.5.27, labelled security) was merged by renovate[bot] itself with no human and no soak. That inheritance is also the escape hatch, and it works in the right direction: a consuming repo that must not automerge adds a trailing packageRule matching every update type, which resolves BEFORE this object is layered on and therefore does reach security updates — platform-infra relies on exactly that to keep production infrastructure off automerge. Setting automerge explicitly here would override that rule and silently re-enable automerge into prod infrastructure, which is why it stays unset.
